summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, morbid obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, and chronic pulmonary emboli was admitted for progressively severe shortness of breath, chest pressure, and a productive cough. Initial evaluation ruled out pulmonary embolism but revealed worsening interstitial lung disease. Her symptoms were attributed to a flare of polymyositis with lung involvement and possible respiratory infection, though extensive microbiologic testing did not confirm an active infection. She was treated with high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone, transitioned to oral steroids, and received a rituximab infusion. Her anticoagulation was managed with heparin bridging and warfarin restart after a bronchoscopy. Iron supplementation was initiated for iron deficiency anemia. By discharge, her respiratory status improved, oxygen requirements decreased to nighttime use, and she was able to ambulate with assistance. She was discharged on increased prednisone, daily Bactrim, iron, and warfarin, with plans for outpatient pulmonary function tests and rheumatology follow-up including a second rituximab infusion.
